Briefing for 15 November 2026

Short items for 15 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

In the background

Banks reject Chinese orders for Anthropic's IPO

Bloomberg reports that several banks are turning away orders from mainland China and Hong Kong, partly citing US export rules. Pricing is set for November 18, followed by Nasdaq trading under the ticker ANT.

Source: The Decoder

AI agents

FBI warns of an open-source AI hacking framework

The FBI says attackers are using ARTEX, which turns a language model into an automated attack tool. In some intrusions, it took under three hours to get from first targeting to privileged access.

Source: The Record

Everyday tool

Gemini can now analyze your Google Wallet spending

All Gemini app users in the US can connect Google Wallet and ask about budgets, spending or forgotten subscriptions. Bank and card accounts can optionally be linked through Plaid.

Source: Google

Device

Nvidia board sounds out Arm CEO as Huang successor

According to the Financial Times, Nvidia's board approached Arm chief Rene Haas as one of several candidates to replace Jensen Huang. Nothing is agreed, and finance chief Colette Kress remains interim CEO.

Source: CNA (Reuters)

Device

OpenAI folds its robotics team into research

OpenAI dissolved its standalone robotics team and moved the researchers into its main research and applied groups. It wants general-purpose models to control robots and calls the move a reorganization, not a retreat.

Source: Fortune

AI agents

LangChain raises $300 million at a $3 billion valuation

The Series C was led by CapitalG, with GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP and Sapphire Ventures joining. LangChain says more than 7,000 organizations use its LangSmith platform to run and monitor agents.

Source: LangChain

In the background

llama.cpp reaches version 1.0 with a stable API

The widely used library for running models locally shipped its first stable major release. From now on, changes that break its interface get a new major version number, so apps built on it can rely on it more safely.

Source: Hugging Face

Everyday tool

Cursor explains how its extension marketplace was hit

An access key leaked at vendor Fireworks led an attacker into Cursor systems and to a tampered Claude Code extension that up to 5,000 users may have received. Cursor says most customers were unaffected.

Source: Cursor

Be brave. Get smart.
